{{nihongo|'''Araho Shrine'''|荒穂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hizen Province]].

**Araho Shrine** (あらほじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Kiyama, Saga|arz|كياما|ceb|Kiyama Chō|fa|کیاما، ساگا|fr|Kiyama|id|Kiyama, Saga|it|Kiyama|ja|基山町|ko|기야마정|ms|Kiyama, Saga|pl|Kiyama|ru|Кияма|sv|Kiyama|tl|Kiyama, Saga|tr|Kiyama|uk|Кіяма|ur|کیاما، ساگا|vi|Kiyama, Saga|zh|基山町|qid=Q1206602}}, {{ill|Miyaki District, Saga|fr|District de Miyaki|id|Distrik Miyaki, Saga|it|Distretto di Miyaki|ja|三養基郡|ko|미야키군|pl|Powiat Miyaki|zh|三養基郡|qid=Q1043864}}, {{ill|Saga Prefecture|Q160420|qid=Q160420}}. It is enshrined in the Miyawaki area of Miyaura on the southern foothills of {{ill|Mount Kizan|ja|基山|qid=Q61679989}}.<ref name="kiyama29">[https://www.town.kiyama.lg.jp/kiji003915/3_915_5_7722.pdf The Goshinkō Festival of Araho Shrine] Kōhō Kiyama (Sept. 15, Heisei 29), Kiyama Town</ref> Its shrine rank is that of a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=minor shrine}} listed in the Engishiki, and it later held the status of a {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} under the modern shrine ranking system.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1056017}} along with deities of six other subsidiary shrines.<ref name="kiyamakiji">[https://www.town.kiyama.lg.jp/kiji0031991/index.html Araho Shrine] (November 28, 2018), Kiyama Town</ref>

There have been various theories since ancient times regarding the identity of the enshrined deities, but in folklore studies it is considered that the original deity was Araho Tenjin, a natural and musubi (creative life-force) deity, with the Tamadama Stone—a massive granite boulder at the summit of Mount Kii (Mount Kiyama)—serving as an iwakura (sacred rock).<ref name="kiyama29" /><ref name="kiyamakiji" /> According to the *Araho Shrine Engi* from the first year of Jōkyō (1684), the six shrines are listed as follows: at the center, Araho Daimyōjin; to the left, Shimogamo Ōkami; left second, {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman Ōkami|qid=Q261637}}; to the right, Hōman Ōkami; right second, {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|qid=Q11088805|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805|lt=Kasuga Daimyōjin}}; and right third, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sumiyoshi Daimyōjin}}. (After this, {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|Isotakeru-no-kami|zh|五十猛神|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}} was added.)<ref name="kiyamakiji" />

=== History ===
According to the *Araho Shrine Engi*, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|ar|الإمبراطور كوتوكو|arz|الامبراطور كوتوكو|azb|کوتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Котаку|ca|Kōtoku Tennō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆتۆکو|cs|Kótoku|de|Kōtoku|es|Kōtoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور کوتوکو|fr|Kōtoku|id|Kaisar Kōtoku|it|Kōtoku|ja|孝徳天皇|ka|კოტოკუ|ko|고토쿠 천황|mr|कोतोकू|nl|Kotoku|pl|Kōtoku|pt|Kotoku|ru|Император Котоку|sh|Car Kōtoku|simple|Emperor Kōtoku|sl|Cesar Kotoku|sv|Kotoku|th|จักรพรรดิโคโตกุ|tl|Emperador Kōtoku|tr|Kōtoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Котоку|uz|Imperator Kōtoku|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōtoku|wuu|孝德天皇|yo|Emperor Kōtoku|zh|孝德天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôtoku Thian-hông|zh_yue|孝德天皇|qid=Q317980}} (mid-7th century) by Kanemura no Omi, a descendant of Mononobe no Kanetsura, the provincial governor of Matsura (Kii).<ref name="kiyamakiji" />

The *{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}* records that in the second year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} ({{ill|860|Q24714|qid=Q24714}}), the shrine was promoted in rank from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade.<ref>Entry dated February 8.</ref> It is also one of the four shrines of {{ill|Hizen Province|Q906926|qid=Q906926}} listed in the *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}* (the list of Shikinai shrines of Hizen Province).<ref name="kiyama29" /> The shrine buildings were originally located on the summit of Mount The shrine buildings are constructed in the nagare-zukuri style. === Festivals and rites ===
* New Year’s Day Festival – January 1  
* Spring Festival – February 19  
* Sai Festival – May 1 for seven days  
* Summer Festival – July 19  
* Chinowa purification rite – from July 31 for three days  
* Goshinkō Festival – September 23  

* Monthly Festival – 19th of every month
